brief: git worktree and git rerere: drive the git CLI; b4: drive the git and kernel tools it wraps, not b4 - rhizoid's code is only what no tool has.
decision: git worktree: drive the git CLI (git worktree add --detach, lock --reason, remove), behind rhizoid's GitPort. git rerere: drive the git CLI - assemble is git merge with rerere.enabled and rerere.autoUpdate, stopping when a conflict is left. b4: none of the three as b4 - drive the git and kernel-tree tools it wraps: git format-patch --cover-letter -vN --base to cut a series, git range-diff, the kernel's get_maintainer.pl for recipients, checkpatch.pl for checks; collecting trailers from lore and sending stay out of rhizoid (the author sends), and the branch shape stays b4-compatible so the author may use b4 himself. Rhizome stays the direction, not a dependency: nothing here waits on it. The rule under all three: rhizoid's own code is the part no tool has - the list, the order, the tags, the refusal to edit an int/ branch by hand, the reproduction check, the output for records; git's own work is git's. A cutting (rhizcut) with wrapping code becomes the road when a needed library lacks one small thing and its upstream wants it - the first candidate: gix worktree add/lock, offered upstream. Kept open: gix's in-memory merge_commits as a dry run naming the two conflicting topics before touching a worktree, a later item only if it pays.
why: The author's words of 2026-11-23: "we dont want to reinvent a where where its not needed, unless it gives better quality, simplicity, elegancy, and we could weigh the possibility of using them as rhizcuts instead of driving them through cli's". So each tool was weighed three ways: drive the CLI, take it as a rhizcut used as a library, or write our own. Coverage checked 2026-11-23 against gix 0.85.0, git2 0.21.0 / libgit2 1.9.7 and git 2.56.1 (upstream roadmaps not checked, not known yet) (sources gitoxide, git2-rs, git-rerere): list worktrees - git yes, gix yes (worktrees(), proxies), libgit2 yes; add/lock/unlock worktree - git yes, gix no (read only), libgit2 yes (WorktreeAddOptions::lock, lock, unlock, prune); merge commits/trees - git yes, gix yes in memory (merge_commits, merge_trees), libgit2 yes; rerere (.git/rr-cache) - git yes, gix no, libgit2 no; rebase onto another base - git yes, gix no, libgit2 basic without rerere; format-patch with cover letter and --base - git yes, gix no, libgit2 one patch at a time (git_email_create), no cover letter, no --base; range-diff - git yes, gix no, libgit2 no. rhizoid already drives the git CLI behind GitPort (crates/rhizoid-cli/src/git_repos.rs, rhizoid main 0ffb48a). Worktree: git2 could do it, but would add libgit2 - C, a second git implementation whose worktree files must agree with the CLI's that people and prune use - for three calls; gix cannot add or lock today. Rerere: its point is one memory shared by every hand on the one kernel clone - the builder's git, the author's git, rhizoid; only git's own rerere reads and writes that rr-cache, and a second implementation must hash conflicts exactly as git does or it silently misses, or replays a wrong resolution; neither gix nor libgit2 has it. b4: what we need of it is git's or the kernel tree's own tools; b4 is Python (practice 21).
rejected: git worktree: a gix cutting adding worktree add/lock (worth offering upstream as a pull request, not carrying); our own (it would rewrite .git/worktrees/ by hand); git2/libgit2 as a library (a second C git implementation for three calls). git rerere: a gix cutting with a gix-rerere crate (a large exact-compatibility port, with no upstream to stay in step with); our own (the same, worse). b4: driving b4 (Python, practice 21; already rejected as a requirement in linux-phone-oco/docs decision 2026-11-23-structure-kernel-topics-and-integration); a b4 cutting as a library (Python cannot be a Rust library); a Rust rewrite of b4 (reinvention without gain: the parts we need are git's).
about: rhizoid's kernel flows for linux-phone-oco: assembling test kernels from topic branches, topic and fork status, cutting series versions for upstream

brief: rhizoid carries the git work of linux-phone-oco's structure, generic: assemble, status over kernel edges, send-back, fork to upstream in its graph file.
decision: rhizoid carries the git work of linux-phone-oco's structure, generic (no tad, no phones): assemble (list -> int/ tag), status over topic, backport, int and fork edges, send-back (series version; never signs, sends or pushes), fork -> upstream in its graph file. It owns the list format; each lab owns its file. Callers keep their record checks (lab-tools: upstream-item row, FROMLIST). Worktrees at ${AGENT_WORKTREES:-~/.local/share/agent-worktrees}/REPO/rhizoid/NAME, held with git worktree lock, never elsewhere.
why: The author asked (2026-11-23) that the git flows run on rhizoid; rhizoid's cutting, tracking-vs-patch and clean-patch-back are that layout; the roles' answers in the rhizoid lane's needs draft (walleye, surya, upstreams, ideal-agent, orchestration); linux-phone-oco/docs decision 2026-11-23-structure-git-flows-run-on-rhizoid.
rejected: The merge loop in lab-tools (a second git tool); rhizoid reading tad records (it stays generic and prints what a record command takes); forks in lab.toml [clones] (two places, one fact); worktrees via agent-env's branch (a shell function, not callable from a program); lab-only dts laid in by rhizoid (the tree must equal its tag; the build script keeps them).
about: linux-phone-oco's git flows: kernel topics, integration and sending upstream

brief: The backlog order becomes assemble, status over kernel edges, send-back, pins in one place, then follow, slice-consumption, rhizcut, cutting-as-cargo-dependency.
decision: The order becomes: assemble (assemble-from-list), status over kernel edges (status-over-kernel-edges), send-back (send-back-writes-the-upstream-item), pins in one place (followers-one-pin-bump), then follow-by-conformance, slice-consumption, rhizcut, cutting-as-cargo-dependency - the backlog's rank 2 to 9.
why: Phone lanes wait on assemble and status; the author (2026-11-23): when walleye resumes "depends on what quality we can acheive with git-rhizoid". send-back's need is now concrete (the upstreams lane's answer). Rests on decision 2026-11-23-rhizoid-carries-the-structure-git-flows and linux-phone-oco/docs decision 2026-11-23-structure-git-flows-run-on-rhizoid.
rejected: Keeping the unpark order of 2026-11-18 (status, follow, send-back, cuttings): follow serves idealkb's slices, which have a working shell today; the kernel flows have no tool.

brief: rhizoid holds no default path, names, tag pattern or branch scheme of any one project in code: list files and graphs name them; the kernel layout is an example.
decision: No default path, names, tag pattern or branch scheme of any one project in code. assemble's list file is a required argument (--lists, or RHIZOID_LISTS); it names its own optional name (device is read as name, for files labs already wrote), its tag template (tag = "int/{name}/{list}/{base}/{n}" only as the default) and the branch patterns its lists may name (none: any branch). status reads an [[integration]] edge whose scheme, topics and the shape of assembled tags are the graph's data. ABOUT and the README say what rhizoid is for any repository; linux-phone-oco's kernel layout is an example in examples/ (kernel-topics.toml, kernel.graph.toml).
why: The author asked (2026-11-23, relayed by the rhizoid lane coordinator): "rhizoid is a general tool, not bound to only kernel ?" - it is, and must stay so. The Top Coordinator found three places in v0.1.1 that assumed kernels or devices: the default list path kernel/topics.toml, ABOUT's "assemble test kernels", and the hard-wired int/{device}/{list}/{base}/ tag with a device field.
rejected: Kernel defaults kept for convenience (they bind the tool to one user); a built-in kernel profile or subcommand (the same, hidden); a required device field (a name is optional, and only a tag template may use it).

brief: Each pin stays in the file its reader reads (idealkb.toml for follow, lab.toml for lpoco-host, Cargo.toml for cargo); rhizoid bump lists them in one place rather than one file holding them all.
decision: No follower-wide pin file. A pin stays where the tool that uses it reads it: a slice's in its pin file (idealkb.toml, devicebase.toml), which follow reads and moves; a tool's in its key or line (lab.toml's tools.lpoco, a Cargo git tag), which its installer or cargo reads. The one place is rhizoid bump: every pin of the graph listed together, read where it lives, and moved there. The author's go, 2026-11-23: "ok, it sounds reasonable, if it does not introduce drift and busy work, then ok". His condition is the decision's test: rhizoid bump stays the only thing that moves pins - no second copy of any pin, no hand edit anyone must keep in sync. If building it shows drift or extra work, it goes back to the author through the top coordinator, never a workaround.
why: slice-consumption asked for one pin file the follower owns, for every kind. By the time it was built every kind had a reader that reads its own file - follow.sh and rhizoid follow, lpoco-host, cargo - and none of them reads a second file; a follower-wide file would hold each version twice, and the two would drift. rhizoid bump already gives what the one file was for: every pin seen together, and moved by one command.
rejected: A follower-wide pin file read by rhizoid (two places, one fact: the reader's file and rhizoid's would drift); a pin file that the readers are changed to read (it would bind lpoco-host and cargo and idealkb to rhizoid's format, for no gain over listing).

brief: A cutting is recorded in the repository graph, as its [[fork]] edge with patches and added; rhizoid.toml, its manifest and init are retired.
decision: The repository graph is the one record of a cutting: its [[fork]] edge (fork, upstream, tracking branch, upstream branch) also says patches - one branch, rhizoid/patch unless named, or integration, the topics the repository's [[integration]] edge assembles - and added (add or import); the graph may name fork_org, where add forks to. rhizoid.toml, its [[module]] manifest and rhizoid init are retired; graphs of v0.2.x read unchanged, their [[fork]] edges forks and not yet cuttings. .rhizoid/module.toml stays on a one-branch cutting's patch branch, the fork's own record; an integration cutting has none.
why: The rhizoid lane coordinator (2026-11-23), reading rhizcut's design: the graph already says fork -> upstream ([[fork]] edges; linux-phone-oco/docs decision 2026-11-23-structure-git-flows-run-on-rhizoid; docs' rhizoid.graph.toml), so a rhizoid.toml [[module]] list would say the same fact twice. And the first real cuttings (linux-phone-oco/linux, sxmo-utils) keep their changes as topic branches assembled by an [[integration]] edge, never on one patch branch.
rejected: Two files, rhizoid.toml beside the graph (one fact in two places, which drift); one patch branch for every cutting (a kernel's changes are topics, assembled by the integration edge); a .rhizoid/module.toml required in every fork (an integration cutting pushes nothing to its fork).
supersedes: concepts manifest-file-format and fork-destination-manifest, for where a cutting is recorded

brief: Every pin has exactly one mover, named on its edge, and every mover pushes (a timer that lands through the follower's checks); the graph covers a pin table whole; declared own files read as declared.
decision: (1) One mover per pin, named on its edge: moved_by on [[tool]] and [[slice]] (the slices: idealkb-update-pins; tad: tad-update-pins; lab.toml tools.lpoco: lpoco-host-follow; default: rhizoid-bump). bump now moves only the edges whose mover is rhizoid-bump, and lists the rest with their mover. This amends 2026-11-23-pins-stay-with-their-readers: the one place to see every pin is still bump, but the one mover of a pin is the job its edge names, never two. (2) bump pushes too, the same way the other three do: bump now --land runs the graph's [bump] land argv (here ["land"]) on each bumped branch, so a bump lands when the follower's checks pass, and a failed gate or check leaves the one PR a person sees. rhizoid ships a user service and timer (packaging/systemd, hourly, rhizoid bump now --fetch --land on the graph) on idealkb-update-pins' pattern. Orchestration enables it on the lab host. (3) The graph covers a pin table whole: [[pins]] names a follower's file and table (lab.toml [tools]; a Cargo.toml's git dependencies), and status's pin-coverage check calls a key in it that no edge covers and no unpinned entry (with its why) excuses moved-by-hand, naming the key. A new pin is then a finding at the next status, which patrol runs each round. (4) status reads a slice follower's own and [why] as declared (idealkb decision 2026-11-23-own-files-read-as-declared): a file with a reason is current, with a note when the release changed it, and only an unlisted differing file is moved by hand. The test is the author's condition: no person runs bump, status shows no standing line for anything declared, and a pin is behind for no longer than one period of its mover.
why: The author, 2026-11-23, accepted pins-stay-with-their-readers on his condition 'if it does not introduce drift and busy work, then ok' and then asked why it was not met. Each gap got a fix after the fact: the tools.rhizoid edge, patrol watching behind pins, the idealkb noise. Research 2026-11-23-why-pins-drift-research: three of four pin kinds already push by timer, the fourth, rhizoid bump, is pull; nothing compares pin files with the graph; status reads declared intent as drift. Renovate, Dependabot and update-flake-lock make behind a passing state by schedule plus landing on green.
rejected: bump as the one mover everywhere: lpoco-host-follow must install before it lands the pin (the pin is the record of what runs), and idealkb-update-pins also lays files; replacing two working conveyors is churn. A release hook in each source's CI: a token into every follower from every source and config per source, while the lab already runs three timers. Renovate with regex managers or Dependabot: a new tool and service for what bump already does; Dependabot cannot read our pin files. GitHub auto-merge on bump PRs: our changes land through land (practice 7). Generating edges by scanning pin files, as Renovate's managers do: a key cannot say its source or tag scheme (tools.land and agent-env pin git revs, oco-work is unknown); a coverage check with declared exceptions covers a new pin without guessing. A suppress list inside rhizoid: a second place for what idealkb.toml already says.
